results.requestText: It's raining all day and I'll be walking a lot. What should I wear?

checks.detail: Shares most of its clothing with look 1.

looks.title: Gig Fit, Rain Edition
looks.idea: Your favourite gig formula, because the short hem stays clear of puddles and the bike chain while tights and boots keep your legs covered and warm.
looks.howToWear: Pull the hoodie on over the tights and let it fall to mid-hip so the tartan hem shows just below it. Zip the cropped puffer over the top. Pull the hoodie hood out over the puffer collar and up on the walk, then down on the bike so you can see. Lace the boots tight for the pedals. Wear the chain over the hoodie, under the puffer.
looks.why: This is your proven favourite: an oversized top over a short A-line skirt, which is the proportion you like. The mini clears wet ground and can't catch on the bike. The 80 denier tights, wool skirt, fleece hoodie and puffer give real warmth at 3°C. The chunky leather boots can handle wet pavements and grip the pedals. Red tartan and black suit your colouring. Caveat: nothing in your wardrobe is rain-ready. The puffer is not rain-ready, so in steady rain the hoodie and skirt will get damp, and the hoodie will get heavy. The wool and fleece will still hold some warmth.)

looks.title: Undone Utility
looks.idea: Black cargos, a faded band tee and a grey hoodie: the Berlin studio-to-bar uniform, with the trouser hems tucked away from the wet.
looks.howToWear: Wear the band tee as the base and let its faded hem peek out under the hoodie. Tuck the cargo hems into the boots and lace tight, so nothing hangs near the chain or pedals and the twill can't drag in puddles. Zip the cropped puffer over the top, which keeps the shape short over the oversized hoodie. Wear the chain over the hoodie, under the puffer.
looks.why: The cargos give full leg coverage, and tucked into the boots they can't drag on wet ground or catch on the bike, which the baggy jeans' low-slung hems would. The tee under the hoodie adds a layer without bulk, and the oversized hoodie with relaxed trousers and a cropped jacket is the undone, music-led look you like. It is close to your everyday uniform, so it is the easy option. Caveat: the twill will soak in steady rain and the puffer is not rain-ready. Legs will be less warm than in a skirt with 80 denier tights, so this is the more practical look but not the warmest.

looks.title: Tartan and Forest
looks.idea: Forest green knit over red tartan, held together by black tights, boots and puffer: a deliberate deep-colour grunge pairing that gets the skirt out more.
looks.howToWear: Pull the chunky jumper down loose so its hem hangs below the cropped puffer, with a flash of tartan showing beneath it. Zip the puffer fully to cover as much of the knit as possible and push the sleeves up. Wear the black tights and lace the boots tight. Wear the chain over the knit, under the puffer.
looks.why: Forest green and red both suit your colouring against black hair and fair skin, and the black tights, boots and puffer tie the two together on purpose. The oversized knit over a short skirt is the proportion you like, and the mini clears puddles and the bike chain. The green jumper is the warmest top you own and the tartan skirt has only been worn 6 times. Caveat: cable-knit wool soaks up rain and the puffer is not rain-ready, so this is the weakest look in constant rain. If it is steady all day, swap the jumper for the grey hoodie, as in Look 1.

output.note: Nothing in your wardrobe is rain-ready: the puffer, leather jacket and white trainers are all flagged as not suited to sustained rain. I used the puffer in all three because it is the warmest layer you have, and it will only take the edge off, not keep you dry. I left out the leather jacket, the suede and leather trainers, the slip dress (delicate, thin, risky on the bike) and the baggy jeans (low-slung hems that would soak and drag). The real gap is a waterproof, hooded shell. Until you have one, get in out of the rain quickly, and don't count on the canvas tote keeping anything dry.

rules: It is 3°C and cold rain all day (cold).
Every look needs outerwear for getting there and back, and the whole look must be warm enough for the time spent outside.

Sustained rain: outerwear must be rain-ready, shoes must cope with wet ground, and avoid delicate fabrics (suede, velvet, silk) where they will get wet. Full-length hems will drag and wick on wet ground unless they clear the shoe.
The client cycles today: no long or loose hems that can catch, no coats that tangle on the bike, shoes that grip the pedals.
Lots of walking: comfortable shoes the client can walk in all day.

draftViolations: Look 1: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.
Look 2: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.
Look 3: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.

issues.detail: The draft claims the puffer's hood sits 'out over the collar', but l10 is a cropped puffer with no hood listed. Also, all-day cold rain with only a non-rain-ready puffer means a damp hoodie and skirt. Nothing in the wardrobe is rain-ready, so this is a wardrobe gap, not a failure of the look, but the explanation must not overstate protection.
issues.fix: Remove the hood instruction; say the hoodie hood goes up under or over the puffer collar. Keep l10 as the best available outer layer and state plainly that it will only shed light rain.

issues.detail: The 'bare ankles' idea in the Idea line is untrue: the look uses opaque tights and boots, so no ankles are bare. Also, 'nothing is rain-ready' contradicts the claim of staying clear of puddles being the main benefit.
issues.fix: Reword the idea: the short hem clears puddles and the bike chain; tights and boots keep legs warm.

issues.detail: Explanation includes untrue or sloppy claims (bare ankles, puffer hood). The tights under a wet-prone mini skirt will wick, but fine overall.
issues.fix: Correct the idea and styling text as above; the outfit itself is the client's proven favourite and works.

issues.detail: Tucking cargo hems into lace-up boots is a good technique for rain and cycling, but the draft offers two options and the 'catch in the chain' remark is loose. Tucked cargos plus oversized hoodie under a cropped puffer is the right proportion; nothing else is wrong.
issues.fix: Commit to one: tuck the cargo hems into the boots (l11) and lace tight so nothing hangs near the chain or pedals.

issues.detail: Claims the cargos are the warmest bottoms that work today, which is not true compared with a mini skirt and 80 denier tights (l07 + l13), and says the twill dries faster than denim without basis it needs to state. Also the look is very close to the client's everyday uniform.
issues.fix: Say cargos are a practical, full-coverage option that is less drag-prone than jeans when tucked; drop the 'warmest' claim. Add the tee-peek and chain styling as the finishing touch.

issues.detail: The explanation says the puffer is 'snug' over the chunky knit and that the look suits light rain only; cable-knit wool soaks up rain and holds water, so it is the weakest choice for a day of constant rain. The idea (green and red) is strong and uses an under-worn piece.
issues.fix: Keep the look but be honest: sustained rain will soak the knit. Suggest zipping the puffer fully to cover the knit and keeping the hoodie l01 in the tote as a dry swap, or swap l04 for l01 if rain is constant.

issues.detail: A big cable knit pulled loose over a mini with a cropped puffer on top can bulk the upper body and hide the skirt; the puffer is snug over the knit.
issues.fix: Push the puffer sleeves up, leave it open at the hem, and let a flash of tartan show below the knit so the proportion reads oversized-on-short.

issues.detail: The idea says 'slightly clashing', but deep green and red tartan with black base is deliberate and works on her colouring. It just needs an anchor.
issues.fix: Describe it as a deliberate tartan-with-forest-green pairing tied together by black tights, boots and puffer.

critique.overall: The set is coherent and on-brand, and all three looks are workable for walking and cycling, but the range is narrow: all share the same puffer, boots, chain and tote, and two are the same skirt. The real gap is a waterproof shell, which should be flagged to the client; none of the pieces beat the current picks for today.

finalViolations: Look 1: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.
Look 2: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.
Look 3: Sustained rain but no rain-ready outerwear.

failures.detail: After a full day of walking in 3°C rain, nylon tights (l13) under a mini (l07) will be wet against the skin, and the stylist doesn't flag this. The hoodie (l01) hem below the cropped puffer (l10) will also soak and stay cold. It is workable, but the leg warmth claimed for 'real warmth at 3°C' overstates what you get in all-day rain.
This is her known gig outfit with the puffer added. Using a proven win is reasonable, but the look adds no new idea beyond the rain notes.
'Pull the hoodie on over the tights' is a garbled instruction. Hiding the chain (l14) under a zipped puffer makes it nearly pointless outdoors.

looks.comment: This is the right instinct: her proven formula, with the hoodie hood out over the puffer collar as her only head cover. That is the smartest practical move in the whole set. The look is honest about the rain, but it is essentially a repeat.

failures.detail: The obvious move was missed: the 80-denier tights (l13) should go under the cargos (l06) as a base layer. That makes this the warmest legwear option, and the second layer still insulates once the twill is wet.

The claim that legs are 'less warm than in a skirt with 80 denier tights' is dubious. Full-length twill is generally warmer than tights plus a mini, and this claim could steer her to the wrong look in the rain.

Relaxed cargos tucked into ankle-height boots (l11) will bunch and balloon at the ankle. Rolling or cuffing them would be cleaner. She also asked for oversized tops balanced with something fitted or short, and an oversized hoodie over relaxed trousers only gets that balance from the cropped puffer.
This is an all grey-and-black everyday uniform with the same hoodie-plus-puffer top half as Look 1. The tee (l02) under the hoodie is invisible except for a hem flash.

looks.comment: This is the most practical base for a long wet walk, and the hood stays in play. However, it's under-thought: no tights underneath, a shaky tuck, and an explanation that gets the warmth comparison backwards.

failures.detail: There is no hood anywhere in the look, so her head is uncovered in all-day 3°C rain. The cable knit (l04) hanging below the cropped puffer will act like a sponge.
'Push the sleeves up' in cold rain leaves forearms or knit cuffs exposed and wet, which actively undermines warmth.
A forest cable jumper over red tartan leans festive and preppy unless it is roughed up. Only the chain is doing that, and it is hidden under the puffer.
The stylist calls it the weakest look in constant rain and suggests swapping the jumper for the hoodie, which turns it back into Look 1. If it's wrong for today, don't send it today.

looks.comment: Green against red is a genuine colour idea for her contrast colouring, and it gets the under-worn skirt out. But this is a dry-day look, and the stylist knew it and sent it for a rain brief anyway.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The best rain look layers rather than swaps. Put the tights (l13) under the cargos (l06), with cuffs rolled to boot height and laced tight in l11. Then the white ribbed tank (l03) as a base, the green jumper (l04) worn under the grey hoodie (l01) only if it isn't too bulky (otherwise the band tee, l02), with the hood up and out over the zipped puffer (l10). Add the chain (l14) and the tote (l15), lined with a plastic bag. Warm, hooded, bikeable, still grunge.
judgement.summary: The stylist is honest about the real gap: there is no waterproof shell. They correctly choose the puffer and boots throughout and rightly drop the slip dress and the low-slung jeans. However, all three looks share the same outer layer, shoes, bag and jewellery, so the range is thin. Look 3 is admitted to be wrong for the day. The most useful technique, tights as a base layer under trousers, is missed, and the explanation misjudges which look is warmer. Look 1 is sendable. Looks 2 and 3 need reworking before they go out.

results.requestText: I'm presenting to senior leadership next week. I want to look authoritative but still like me.

checks.detail: Shares most of its clothing with look 1.
Shares most of its clothing with look 1.
Shares most of its clothing with look 2.

looks.title: Tartan Authority
looks.idea: Slouchy knit over a sharp tartan mini, all in deep colours and anchored by black boots: authority with an edge.
looks.howToWear: Half-tuck the front of the green jumper into the skirt so the waist shows and the knit stays oversized. Wear the black tights and lace-up boots, with the laces tight and neat. Put the leather jacket on over the jumper and leave it open. Wear the chain outside the jumper's neckline. Carry the tote across your body for the ride.
looks.why: This is the closest her wardrobe gets to 'senior leadership' while staying hers. Tartan wool, forest green and black all suit her high-contrast colouring, and the green sits near her face. The oversized top with a short fitted bottom is her preferred proportion. The jumper (warmth 4) with the jacket, 80 denier tights and boots is warm enough for 4°C and wind, and the A-line mini and chunky soles are fine on a bike. It builds on her favourite gig outfit, but the jumper replaces the hoodie to read more serious.

looks.title: Green Knit, Tartan Edge
looks.idea: The deep green knit is the colour moment, with the tartan mini and black legs and boots underneath. The puffer is just for the ride, so the knit and chain are what leadership sees.
looks.howToWear: Push the jumper sleeves to the elbow and half-tuck just the front into the tartan skirt, so the knit stays oversized over the short fitted skirt. Wear the black tights and lace-up boots, laces tight and neat. Wear the chain outside the neckline, over the knit. Ride in the cropped puffer, which ends above the skirt hem and stays clear of the saddle, with the tote across your body. At the venue, take the puffer off and either stuff it into the tote or hang it up, so you present in the jumper, skirt and chain.
looks.why: The puffer (warmth 5) is the warmest layer she owns for a cold, windy ride, and its cropped length keeps it out of the bike. Once it's off, the wool jumper, tartan and silver chain read deliberate: no logos, no graphics, and forest green is one of her best colours near her face. The half-tuck keeps her preferred oversized-over-short proportion. The tights (80 denier) and boots keep her legs warm, and the chunky soles grip the pedals. This look shares its base with Look 1; the difference is the puffer for the ride and the jumper being the only layer when she presents.

looks.title: Leather Closed
looks.idea: The vintage leather jacket, fastened, as the serious layer: a more buttoned-up, structured take on the same base, with her own history in it.
looks.howToWear: Half-tuck the front of the green jumper into the tartan skirt, then fasten the leather jacket so its hip-length hem sits over the jumper and the knit doesn't hang below it. Push the jacket sleeves up slightly so the jumper cuffs show, and let the green collar and the chain sit at the neckline. Wear the black tights and lace-up boots with the laces tight and neat. Carry the tote across your body for the ride, and keep the jacket on while you present.
looks.why: Closed, the boxy vintage leather gives a more contained, structured outline than the open jacket in Look 1, and it keeps her music-led taste in the room without any graphics. Jumper (warmth 4) under the jacket (warmth 3), with 80 denier tights and the boots, is warm enough for 4°C and wind, and nothing hangs low enough to catch on the bike. Honestly, this is a near-duplicate of Look 1 in pieces; the difference is the fastened jacket and the greater focus on the collar and chain.

output.note: Honest gap: almost everything in this wardrobe is formality 1–2, and her only 3/5 piece (the satin slip dress) is too light for 4°C and risky on a bike. She has one usable top, one usable bottom and one usable pair of shoes today, so the three looks share a base and differ in outerwear and styling. A black blazer, a plain black or white collared shirt or fine-knit top, and straight black trousers would give her real authority for the presentation without losing her style.

rules: It is 4°C and grey and dry, cold wind (cold).
Every look needs outerwear for getting there and back, and the whole look must be warm enough for the time spent outside.
The client cycles today: no long or loose hems that can catch, no coats that tangle on the bike, shoes that grip the pedals.
Target formality for the clothes: 3–4 out of 5.

issues.detail: The idea claims the tights and boots read as one long dark column, but the red tartan skirt sits between the green jumper and the black legs and breaks that line. The title 'Black Column' is untrue for this look.
issues.fix: Rewrite the idea and title to describe what is really there: green knit, tartan mini, black legs and boots. Drop the 'column' claim.

issues.detail: The how-to-wear says the jumper is tucked in, pushed to the elbow, and then the puffer comes off before presenting. A fully tucked oversized knit loses her oversized-over-short proportion, and the look is mostly the same as Look 1 without the jacket.
issues.fix: Use a half-tuck of l04 into l07, as in Look 1, to keep the oversized silhouette. Keep the puffer l10 for the ride only, and wear the chain l14 outside the neckline.

issues.detail: The tote carried across the body with a puffer is workable, but there is no plan for where the puffer goes during the presentation.
issues.fix: Tell her to stuff the puffer into the tote l15 or hang it up at the venue.

issues.detail: Low-top retro trainers (formality 1) with the casual jacket and no chain pull the look to about 1–2/5, below the 3–4 target for presenting to senior leadership. The explanation itself calls it 'the least formal'. It also undercuts the 'authoritative' request.
issues.fix: Swap l12 for the black lace-up boots l11 to get a more serious tone and extra warmth. Add the chain l14 for polish. To keep range from Look 1, change the jacket styling and mood: wear l09 buttoned or closed with the sleeves pushed up, and keep the knit fully visible.

issues.detail: At 4°C with a cold wind, trainers (warmth 2) with a mid-thigh skirt and a short cycle are chilly. The draft's own advice to 'swap to the boots if the wind is biting' hands the decision back to the client when the weather has already decided.
issues.fix: Commit to l11 boots in the look and remove the conditional swap line.

issues.detail: It says the look is 'the same smart base' in a relaxed mood, but with trainers it is no longer smart, and it is nearly identical to Look 1. It also says the tights keep legs warm enough, which is only true with the boots.
issues.fix: Once the boots are in, make the point of difference the closed jacket or a different bag carry (for example the tote over one shoulder), and say honestly that it is a near-duplicate of Look 1.

critique.overall: The set is honest about a wardrobe with only one workable top and bottom, and Look 1 is a strong, on-brief answer. Looks 2 and 3 are near-copies of it, with Look 3 dropping below the target formality. Range could only really improve by adding the blazer, collared shirt and black trousers suggested in the stylist's note.

failures.detail: This is essentially her gig outfit (l07 + l13 + l11) with l04 swapped for l01. It doesn't answer 'authoritative'. A red tartan mini is the lowest-authority bottom she owns for a leadership presentation, while black cargo trousers l06 sit unused.

Forest green cable knit l04 over red/black tartan l07 tips toward a Christmas or school-uniform, preppy read. That is exactly what her DNA rejects, and the brown leather l09 adds a fifth colour story without tying anything together.
The open, warmth-3 leather jacket on a bike at 4°C in a cold wind will let the wind straight in. Fastening it for the ride, or using the puffer l10, would be warmer.
It asserts this is 'the closest her wardrobe gets to senior leadership' without testing the obvious alternative, l06.

looks.comment: Wearable and recognisably Lena, but it's a recycled gig look. The green-on-red-tartan pairing risks reading preppy rather than authoritative.

failures.detail: It uses the same l04 + l07 + l13 + l11 base as Look 1. The only real change is the ride layer, l10.
The same green-knit-over-red-tartan issue remains. With no jacket on while she presents, it's even more exposed: the cable knit plus tartan mini reads collegiate.

looks.comment: This is the most practical of the three. The cropped puffer l10 is right for a windy ride and stays clear of the saddle, and presenting in the knit with the chain l14 is a clear, deliberate decision. Still, a mini is a soft answer to 'authoritative'.

failures.detail: Fastening the boxy hip-length l09 over the chunky oversized cable knit l04 creates a bulky, straining torso. It also hides the half-tuck the styling notes ask for, so the instructions contradict themselves.
Presenting indoors in a fastened leather jacket over a warmth-4 wool jumper will be hot and stiff. Keeping outerwear on reads as 'just arrived', not authoritative.
The stylist admits this is a near-duplicate of Look 1. It adds nothing to the set.

looks.comment: Fastening the jacket doesn't create structure. It compresses a chunky knit into a bulky shape and keeps her in her coat for the presentation. This look should have been replaced.

judgement.missedOpportunity:
The authority look this wardrobe can actually make:
- Forest green jumper l04, half-tucked into the black cargo trousers l06 so the waist shows over a long black leg column.
- Chunky black boots l11 for one dark line from waist to floor.
- Chunky silver chain l14 at the neck.
- Cropped puffer l10 for the ride, taken off to present; the open leather jacket l09 is the alternative.
- Tote l15.
It keeps her oversized-over-relaxed workwear (Our Legacy Work Shop) proportion, puts her best colour at her face, is warm and fine on a bike, and reads far more serious than a tartan mini. A strong second option the stylist dismissed too quickly is the 90s grunge layer: l08 slip dress with l04 worn over it, plus l13 tights, l11 boots and l09 jacket. The midi satin hem is the most 'senior' line she owns, and the tights and jumper make it warm enough.
judgement.summary: The gap note is honest and useful: it names a blazer, a collared or fine-knit top and straight black trousers as real buys. But the core claim that she has 'one usable bottom' is wrong. The black cargo trousers l06 are the obvious authority piece here, and they never appear. As a result, all three looks are the same green-jumper-and-tartan-mini base with a different jacket, so range is effectively zero. That base is her gig outfit, and the red-tartan-with-green-cable pairing drifts toward the preppy she explicitly rejects. Look 2 is the only one worth sending, as the 'most her' option. It should sit alongside an l06 trouser look and possibly the l08 layered slip dress, so Lena gets a real choice of how much authority to dial up. Look 3 should be cut.
